meetora.title: Meetora
meetora.summary: A platform for discovering cafés and event venues by the hour and sending booking requests.
meetora.image_alt: Meetora home page: venue search form for events
meetora.what: A live product that connects people looking for a venue for a birthday, afterwork or brunch with venue owners. The product is live at getmeetora.com.
highlights: Venue search by event type, location and date.
Transparent hourly pricing and quick booking requests.
Secure online payment and a refer-a-friend discount.
notes: A detailed case study is on the way; for now you can explore the live product directly.

ai-lab.title: AI Lab
ai-lab.summary: A streaming assistant powered by Groq, chat with your documents and a text analyzer.
ai-lab.what: An experiment space holding an assistant called BEX, chat with documents and a context analyzer. All of it runs in the browser; no account needed.
highlights: Streaming answers from Llama models on Groq.
Every chat has its own URL; history is stored only in your browser.
Document chat: PDFs or text are split into chunks and the most relevant parts are passed to the model.
Analyzer: splits text into chunks and shows their weight in the context window as a heatmap and graph.
notes: API routes have rate and input limits; the Groq key lives only on the server.
The provider layer is a single file, so switching models means editing one place.

english-path.title: EnglishPath
english-path.summary: Vocabulary from A1 to C1, ten word games, spaced repetition and level-based exams.
english-path.what: A study tool I built for myself while learning English. Flashcards, games and exams share one progress record.
highlights: About 680 words from A1 to C1, each with a Turkish meaning, pronunciation and example sentence.
Ten games: Taboo, Heads Up, Charades, Category Blitz, Passaparola and five solo word games.
Spaced repetition: words you know come back later, words you miss come back soon.
Level-based exam: more than 140 questions from A1 to C1.
notes: Progress is kept only in the browser (localStorage); no account needed.
Word lists were written by hand; if a word appears at two levels, the lower level wins.

booking-demo.title: Booking demo
booking-demo.summary: An appointment flow driven by n8n webhooks: form, validation and workflow.
booking-demo.what: An appointment form for a barber shop. Behind the form, server-side validation and an n8n workflow do the work.
highlights: Service, barber, date and time selection; Turkish phone number validation.
The form posts to a server endpoint, which validates and forwards to the n8n webhook.
Requests are rate limited.
notes: The webhook address is never sent to the browser; it stays on the server.
This is a demo, not connected to a real shop.

finance-bot.title: Finance bot
finance-bot.summary: n8n workflows that pull financial data from external APIs, process it and report on it.
finance-bot.what: Automated data flows I set up to cut manual work. They pull data from external sources, process it and turn it into reports.
highlights: Workflows designed in n8n.
Pulling, transforming and reporting data from external APIs.
notes: It is for personal use, so there is no public link or screenshot.

this-site.title: This site
this-site.summary: My personal space, built with Next.js 16, next-intl and Tailwind 4, where I try everything out.
this-site.what: The site you're looking at. Both a showcase and the place where I try out what I learn.
highlights: Next.js 16 App Router; pages are statically generated.
Turkish and English content; languages without finished translations are hidden from search engines.
Light and dark themes, reduced-motion support, keyboard navigation.
Contact and booking forms are validated on the server and rate limited.
notes: The source code is public on GitHub.
Photos are from Pexels; screenshots are from my own projects.
